# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (open)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | open |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes; the guard test shows its absence merges two assistant replies on Anthropic | open |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | open |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | open |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Kenneth says it was decided against; no commit found yet, HEAD still accepts `set_chat_model` on the active chat | A thinking/effort change also restarts the cache on both providers (gap 6) | needs a pointer |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | open |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | open |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | open |

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

| Task | Session | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

All three sessions are done. Nothing is merged or pushed. The plan doc is updated with their results.

**Measurement** ([session](#local_7bcf5a8e-9d69-46a3-822f-2c343fe5f599), report in [chat-history-measurement.md](chat-history-measurement.md)). The first finding is that no full request body of a live chat exists anywhere. The app has no request-body logging, and the harness cut every stored result at 4,000 characters. So the per-component split at a turn start is inference from token counts, and the report labels it as such. What the data does show:

- The 64 KiB trim never fired. The largest replayed history was about 27 KB.
- The 16 KiB cut probably fired once, on one `object_analyze` result, estimated at 17 to 19 KB.
- Turn-start rewrites were 24% of all cache writes in the baseline run and 3% with the prototype.
- Two leaks the handoff missed. Skill text sits after the moving cache breakpoint, so it is billed uncached and cached one request late. And the tool list changes when a request carries an importable attachment, which on Anthropic voids the whole cache since tools come first. The second is unmeasured.
- A 6-minute pause in one chat expired Anthropic's 5-minute cache and rewrote everything. That was 13 to 21% of that run's cache writes.

**Guard test** ([session](#local_e9deb314-2a0d-40d5-a5e2-54125736b24b), commit 378b3037a0 on `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5`). Two hidden Catch2 cases tagged `[history-prefix]`, both codecs, driving the real host against a fake transport. They fail on HEAD at the first replayed message, which lacks its workspace block. The main case passes with the prototype; the skills case fails exactly where the handoff predicted. The default suite stays green. Its `cache-rules.md` lists nine gaps against the provider docs, with citations.

**Tool-record fix** ([session](#local_b36c90ea-ddca-4ce3-ad0d-3fe4b39cfef5), commit cc5c12f9ff on `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2`). The sequence was confirmed and reproduced, with one extra detail: the model was never told about the failure at all, because the continuation had already been consumed. The fix makes the save part of the call's outcome, announced once, and `fail()` now throws on an announced record. I read the diff. It is small and in the right layer, though it uses both a scope guard and an explicit clear for the same field, which one of them could go. 463 agent cases pass. Seven MCP bridge cases hang on HEAD too and were left out.

**Added to the plan.** Two decisions from the gap list: D7, whether to pay for Anthropic's 1-hour cache given how often people pause, and D8, a per-chat `prompt_cache_key` on OpenAI, which is cheap and has no behaviour change. One step, R0, to merge the two commits after your review. And a note that the harness needs request-body logging before the OpenAI baseline or any phase-2 run, or we will again have only token counts to argue from.

Git history: `git -C /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin log --all -i --grep` for terms like latency, lock, block, "ms", flush, commit cost, persistence, chat document, measured, benchmark, in combination with persistence/chat/document. 2. Memory notes: `ls /Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/` and grep them for persistence/flush/write cost/latency.

Claude Code session transcripts: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin*/*.jsonl` (large files; use `rg -l` with several terms, then `rg -o` with context on the matches; never cat a whole file). 5. `agent-docs/` in the repo for any persistence design doc with numbers.

Do not infer or estimate costs yourself.

# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (open)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | open |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes; the guard test shows its absence merges two assistant replies on Anthropic | open |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | open |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | open |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Kenneth says it was decided against; no commit found yet, HEAD still accepts `set_chat_model` on the active chat | A thinking/effort change also restarts the cache on both providers (gap 6) | needs a pointer |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | open |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | open |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | open |

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

| Task | Session | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Measure recorded requests | `cache-measure` | done | `chat-history-measurement.md`. No full live request bodies exist anywhere (the app has no request-body logging; the harness cut stored results at 4,000 chars). 26 scripted bodies in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` plus Opus usage lines were measured. See findings below. |
| M2 Byte-prefix invariant test + provider cache rules | `cache-invariant` | done | Commit `378b3037a0` on `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5`: two hidden Catch2 cases, tag `[history-prefix]`, both codecs, fail on HEAD (10/102 assertions), main case passes with the prototype, skills case fails where predicted (reminder at front, Responses drops the skill). `cache-rules.md` in that worktree root: cited rules, 9 gaps. Run: `agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`. |
| M3 Fix the Succeeded-to-Failed rewrite (handoff 4.9) | `tool-record-fix` | done, unmerged | Commit `cc5c12f9ff` on `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2`. Reproduced on HEAD. Fix: the save after a change is part of the outcome; the coordinator announces once, after the save; `fail()` throws `logic_error` on an announced record. 463 agent cases pass. 7 MCP bridge cases hang on HEAD too (pre-existing, not touched). |
| M4 Record an OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini) three-chat baseline before any revert | — | not started, needs D6 | Also needs request-body logging in the harness (M1: none exists); add it first so M4 and phase 2 produce bodies, not just usage lines. |

### M1 findings that change the plan

- **Never fired:** the 64 KiB trim. **Probably once:** the 16 KiB cut (bunny `object_analyze`, est. 17–19 KB, inference). Both are deletable without losing anything measured.
- **What actually changes at a turn start** (all inference on the split, no bodies): workspace blocks on each live result (1.0–1.7 KB each, ~60% of in-turn result bytes) and on the person's message; fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB); the plate picture (~1,050 Anthropic tokens); thinking; the reminder flip; the note.
- **Cost of retelling:** turn-start rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run, 3% with the prototype.
- **Two new leak candidates (not in the handoff):**
  - Skill text sits after the moving cache breakpoint, so it is billed uncached and written one request late (2,537 tokens per file-load turn, 441 per setup turn). Fix is a breakpoint placement, independent of the reverts.
  - `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` adds `object_import` only when the request has an importable attachment. On Anthropic tools come first, so a change there voids the whole cache. Not measured; needs a check.
- **Tokens per byte:** 2.7–3.4 bytes/token on this content, not 4; byte estimates understate tokens by 15–35%.

## Phase 1: reverts, one at a time, least behavioural change first

Each step: `[history-prefix]` guard + agent suite; steps that change what the model reads also run
the prompt eval harness on recorded cases. One session at a time on the Agent sources.

| Step | Depends on | Status |
|---|---|---|
| R0 Merge M3 (`cc5c12f9ff`) and the guard test (`378b3037a0`) into `jusprin-newui` | Kenneth's review | not started |
| R1 Stop the file-load reminder flipping | D4 | not started |
| R2 Keep fired skills in the record on both providers; stop dropping them from the next OpenAI request | guard | not started |
| R3 Remove the 64 KiB rolling trim and the 16 KiB result cut; put the real limit in their place | D3 | not started |
| R4 Keep earlier messages' workspace blocks in the record | guard | not started |
| R5 Keep pictures in the record (blob references; ~1,050 Anthropic tokens each) | guard | not started |
| R6 Notes | D2 | not started |
| R7 Store each turn as sent, thinking included; delete the prototype's carry mechanism, keep its test | D1, D5 | not started |
| R8 Cache hygiene from M2 gaps: skill breakpoint placement, `prompt_cache_key` (D8), check `offered_tools` stability | D8 | not started |

## Phase 2: live confirmation (paid, needs D6)

One three-chat batch on Anthropic and one on OpenAI, before and after. Opus baseline exists in
`.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch/opus-batch/out-baseline/`. Measure cache reads vs cache
writes from the usage fields, plus answer quality via the eval harness. Add request-body logging
to the harness first (see M4) so the "after" run can be checked body by body, not only by tokens.

## Branches and worktrees

|---|---|---|
| `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | guard test commit; untracked `cache-rules.md` |
| `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | `.claude/worktrees/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | M3 fix commit |
| `claude/opus-cost-batch` | `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch` | uncommitted prototype + Anthropic harness switch; batch logs under `opus-batch/` |

## Log

- 2026-10-29: plan approved by Kenneth; M1, M2, M3 started as sessions on Opus 5.5.
- 2026-10-29: M1, M2, M3 done. Added D7, D8, R0, R8 from their findings. Nothing merged or pushed.

# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (open)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | open |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes; the guard test shows its absence merges two assistant replies on Anthropic | open |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | open |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | open |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Kenneth says it was decided against; no commit found yet, HEAD still accepts `set_chat_model` on the active chat | A thinking/effort change also restarts the cache on both providers (gap 6) | needs a pointer |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | open |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | open |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | open |

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

| Task | Session | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Measure recorded requests | `cache-measure` | done | `chat-history-measurement.md`. No full live request bodies exist anywhere (the app has no request-body logging; the harness cut stored results at 4,000 chars). 26 scripted bodies in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` plus Opus usage lines were measured. See findings below. |
| M2 Byte-prefix invariant test + provider cache rules | `cache-invariant` | done | Commit `378b3037a0` on `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5`: two hidden Catch2 cases, tag `[history-prefix]`, both codecs, fail on HEAD (10/102 assertions), main case passes with the prototype, skills case fails where predicted (reminder at front, Responses drops the skill). `cache-rules.md` in that worktree root: cited rules, 9 gaps. Run: `agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`. |
| M3 Fix the Succeeded-to-Failed rewrite (handoff 4.9) | `tool-record-fix` | done, unmerged | Commit `cc5c12f9ff` on `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2`. Reproduced on HEAD. Fix: the save after a change is part of the outcome; the coordinator announces once, after the save; `fail()` throws `logic_error` on an announced record. 463 agent cases pass. 7 MCP bridge cases hang on HEAD too (pre-existing, not touched). |
| M4 Record an OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini) three-chat baseline before any revert | — | not started, needs D6 | Also needs request-body logging in the harness (M1: none exists); add it first so M4 and phase 2 produce bodies, not just usage lines. |

### M1 findings that change the plan

- **Never fired:** the 64 KiB trim. **Probably once:** the 16 KiB cut (bunny `object_analyze`, est. 17–19 KB, inference). Both are deletable without losing anything measured.
- **What actually changes at a turn start** (all inference on the split, no bodies): workspace blocks on each live result (1.0–1.7 KB each, ~60% of in-turn result bytes) and on the person's message; fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB); the plate picture (~1,050 Anthropic tokens); thinking; the reminder flip; the note.
- **Cost of retelling:** turn-start rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run, 3% with the prototype.
- **Two new leak candidates (not in the handoff):**
  - Skill text sits after the moving cache breakpoint, so it is billed uncached and written one request late (2,537 tokens per file-load turn, 441 per setup turn). Fix is a breakpoint placement, independent of the reverts.
  - `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` adds `object_import` only when the request has an importable attachment. On Anthropic tools come first, so a change there voids the whole cache. Not measured; needs a check.
- **Tokens per byte:** 2.7–3.4 bytes/token on this content, not 4; byte estimates understate tokens by 15–35%.

## Phase 1: reverts, one at a time, least behavioural change first

Each step: `[history-prefix]` guard + agent suite; steps that change what the model reads also run
the prompt eval harness on recorded cases. One session at a time on the Agent sources.

| Step | Depends on | Status |
|---|---|---|
| R0 Merge M3 (`cc5c12f9ff`) and the guard test (`378b3037a0`) onto a common branch | Kenneth's review | done 2026-10-29: `claude/chat-history-cache` at `7c88fa2143`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache`. Not merged to `jusprin-newui`, not pushed. |
| R1 Stop the file-load reminder flipping | D4 | not started |
| R2 Keep fired skills in the record on both providers; stop dropping them from the next OpenAI request | guard | not started |
| R3 Remove the 64 KiB rolling trim and the 16 KiB result cut; put the real limit in their place | D3 | not started |
| R4 Keep earlier messages' workspace blocks in the record | guard | not started |
| R5 Keep pictures in the record (blob references; ~1,050 Anthropic tokens each) | guard | not started |
| R6 Notes | D2 | not started |
| R7 Store each turn as sent, thinking included; delete the prototype's carry mechanism, keep its test; un-hide the `[history-prefix]` cases (drop the `[.]` tag) so CTest runs them | D1, D5, D9 | not started |
| R8 Cache hygiene from M2 gaps: skill breakpoint placement, `prompt_cache_key` (D8), check `offered_tools` stability | D8 | not started |

## Phase 2: live confirmation (paid, needs D6)

One three-chat batch on Anthropic and one on OpenAI, before and after. Opus baseline exists in
`.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch/opus-batch/out-baseline/`. Measure cache reads vs cache
writes from the usage fields, plus answer quality via the eval harness. Add request-body logging
to the harness first (see M4) so the "after" run can be checked body by body, not only by tokens.

## Branches and worktrees

| Branch | Worktree | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | guard test commit; untracked `cache-rules.md` |
| `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | `.claude/worktrees/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | M3 fix commit |
| `claude/opus-cost-batch` | `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch` | uncommitted prototype + Anthropic harness switch; batch logs under `opus-batch/` |

## Log

- 2026-10-29: M1, M2, M3 done. Added D7, D8, R0, R8 from their findings. Nothing merged or pushed.

# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (open)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | open |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes. Not neutral: the guard test shows that without the note, two consecutive assistant replies merge into one message on Anthropic | open |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | open |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | open |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Kenneth says it was decided against; no commit found yet, HEAD still accepts `set_chat_model` on the active chat | A thinking/effort change also restarts the cache on both providers (gap 6) | needs a pointer |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | open |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | open |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | open |
| D9 | Write cost of a larger chat record | Kenneth asked (2026-10-29) whether the latency / UI lock-up of writing large chat data to disk was ever measured. History search running; result goes here | gates D1 and R7 | searching |

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

| Task | Session | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Measure recorded requests | `cache-measure` | done | `chat-history-measurement.md`. No full live request bodies exist anywhere (the app has no request-body logging; the harness cut stored results at 4,000 chars). 26 scripted bodies in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` plus Opus usage lines were measured. See findings below. |
| M2 Byte-prefix invariant test + provider cache rules | `cache-invariant` | done | Commit `378b3037a0` on `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5`: two hidden Catch2 cases, tag `[history-prefix]`, both codecs, fail on HEAD (10/102 assertions), main case passes with the prototype, skills case fails where predicted (reminder at front, Responses drops the skill). `cache-rules.md` in that worktree root: cited rules, 9 gaps. Run: `agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`. |
| M3 Fix the Succeeded-to-Failed rewrite (handoff 4.9) | `tool-record-fix` | done, unmerged | Commit `cc5c12f9ff` on `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2`. Reproduced on HEAD. Fix: the save after a change is part of the outcome; the coordinator announces once, after the save; `fail()` throws `logic_error` on an announced record. 463 agent cases pass. 7 MCP bridge cases hang on HEAD too (pre-existing, not touched). |
| M4 Record an OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini) three-chat baseline before any revert | — | not started, needs D6 | Also needs request-body logging in the harness (M1: none exists); add it first so M4 and phase 2 produce bodies, not just usage lines. |

### M1 findings that change the plan

- **Never fired:** the 64 KiB trim. **Probably once:** the 16 KiB cut (bunny `object_analyze`, est. 17–19 KB, inference). Both are deletable without losing anything measured.
- **What actually changes at a turn start** (all inference on the split, no bodies): workspace blocks on each live result (1.0–1.7 KB each, ~60% of in-turn result bytes) and on the person's message; fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB); the plate picture (~1,050 Anthropic tokens); thinking; the reminder flip; the note.
- **Cost of retelling:** turn-start rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run, 3% with the prototype.
- **Two new leak candidates (not in the handoff):**
  - Skill text sits after the moving cache breakpoint, so it is billed uncached and written one request late (2,537 tokens per file-load turn, 441 per setup turn). Fix is a breakpoint placement, independent of the reverts.
  - `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` adds `object_import` only when the request has an importable attachment. On Anthropic tools come first, so a change there voids the whole cache. Not measured; needs a check.
- **Tokens per byte:** 2.7–3.4 bytes/token on this content, not 4; byte estimates understate tokens by 15–35%.

## Phase 1: reverts, one at a time, least behavioural change first

Each step: `[history-prefix]` guard + agent suite; steps that change what the model reads also run
the prompt eval harness on recorded cases. One session at a time on the Agent sources.

| Step | Depends on | Status |
|---|---|---|
| R0 Merge M3 (`cc5c12f9ff`) and the guard test (`378b3037a0`) onto a common branch | Kenneth's review | done 2026-10-29: `claude/chat-history-cache` at `7c88fa2143`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache`. Not merged to `jusprin-newui`, not pushed. |
| R1 Stop the file-load reminder flipping | D4 | not started |
| R2 Keep fired skills in the record on both providers; stop dropping them from the next OpenAI request | guard | not started |
| R3 Remove the 64 KiB rolling trim and the 16 KiB result cut; put the real limit in their place | D3 | not started |
| R4 Keep earlier messages' workspace blocks in the record | guard | not started |
| R5 Keep pictures in the record (blob references; ~1,050 Anthropic tokens each) | guard | not started |
| R6 Notes | D2 | not started |
| R7 Store each turn as sent, thinking included; delete the prototype's carry mechanism, keep its test; un-hide the `[history-prefix]` cases (drop the `[.]` tag) so CTest runs them | D1, D5, D9 | not started |
| R8 Cache hygiene from M2 gaps: skill breakpoint placement, `prompt_cache_key` (D8), check `offered_tools` stability | D8 | not started |

## Phase 2: live confirmation (paid, needs D6)

One three-chat batch on Anthropic and one on OpenAI, before and after. Opus baseline exists in
`.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch/opus-batch/out-baseline/`. Measure cache reads vs cache
writes from the usage fields, plus answer quality via the eval harness. Add request-body logging
to the harness first (see M4) so the "after" run can be checked body by body, not only by tokens.

## Branches and worktrees

|---|---|---|
| `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | guard test commit; untracked `cache-rules.md` |

# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (open)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | open |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes. Not neutral: the guard test shows that without the note, two consecutive assistant replies merge into one message on Anthropic | open |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | open |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | open |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Kenneth says it was decided against; no commit found yet, HEAD still accepts `set_chat_model` on the active chat | A thinking/effort change also restarts the cache on both providers (gap 6) | needs a pointer |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | open |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | open |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | open |
| D9 | Write cost of a larger chat record | Kenneth asked (2026-10-29) whether the latency / UI lock-up of writing large chat data to disk was ever measured. History search running; result goes here | gates D1 and R7 | searching |

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

| Task | Session | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Measure recorded requests | `cache-measure` | done | `chat-history-measurement.md`. No full live request bodies exist anywhere (the app has no request-body logging; the harness cut stored results at 4,000 chars). 26 scripted bodies in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` plus Opus usage lines were measured. See findings below. |
| M2 Byte-prefix invariant test + provider cache rules | `cache-invariant` | done | Commit `378b3037a0` on `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5`: two hidden Catch2 cases, tag `[history-prefix]`, both codecs, fail on HEAD (10/102 assertions), main case passes with the prototype, skills case fails where predicted (reminder at front, Responses drops the skill). `cache-rules.md` in that worktree root: cited rules, 9 gaps. Run: `agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`. |
| M3 Fix the Succeeded-to-Failed rewrite (handoff 4.9) | `tool-record-fix` | done, unmerged | Commit `cc5c12f9ff` on `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2`. Reproduced on HEAD. Fix: the save after a change is part of the outcome; the coordinator announces once, after the save; `fail()` throws `logic_error` on an announced record. 463 agent cases pass. 7 MCP bridge cases hang on HEAD too (pre-existing, not touched). |
| M4 Record an OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini) three-chat baseline before any revert | — | not started, needs D6 | Also needs request-body logging in the harness (M1: none exists); add it first so M4 and phase 2 produce bodies, not just usage lines. |

### M1 findings that change the plan

- **Never fired:** the 64 KiB trim. **Probably once:** the 16 KiB cut (bunny `object_analyze`, est. 17–19 KB, inference). Both are deletable without losing anything measured.
- **What actually changes at a turn start** (all inference on the split, no bodies): workspace blocks on each live result (1.0–1.7 KB each, ~60% of in-turn result bytes) and on the person's message; fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB); the plate picture (~1,050 Anthropic tokens); thinking; the reminder flip; the note.
- **Cost of retelling:** turn-start rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run, 3% with the prototype.
- **Two new leak candidates (not in the handoff):**
  - Skill text sits after the moving cache breakpoint, so it is billed uncached and written one request late (2,537 tokens per file-load turn, 441 per setup turn). Fix is a breakpoint placement, independent of the reverts.
  - `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` adds `object_import` only when the request has an importable attachment. On Anthropic tools come first, so a change there voids the whole cache. Not measured; needs a check.
- **Tokens per byte:** 2.7–3.4 bytes/token on this content, not 4; byte estimates understate tokens by 15–35%.

## Phase 1: reverts, one at a time, least behavioural change first

Each step: `[history-prefix]` guard + agent suite; steps that change what the model reads also run
the prompt eval harness on recorded cases. One session at a time on the Agent sources.

| Step | Depends on | Status |
|---|---|---|
| R0 Merge M3 (`cc5c12f9ff`) and the guard test (`378b3037a0`) onto a common branch | Kenneth's review | done 2026-10-29: `claude/chat-history-cache` at `7c88fa2143`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache`. Not merged to `jusprin-newui`, not pushed. |
| R1 Stop the file-load reminder flipping | D4 | not started |
| R2 Keep fired skills in the record on both providers; stop dropping them from the next OpenAI request | guard | not started |
| R3 Remove the 64 KiB rolling trim and the 16 KiB result cut; put the real limit in their place | D3 | not started |
| R4 Keep earlier messages' workspace blocks in the record | guard | not started |
| R5 Keep pictures in the record (blob references; ~1,050 Anthropic tokens each) | guard | not started |
| R6 Notes | D2 | not started |
| R7 Store each turn as sent, thinking included; delete the prototype's carry mechanism, keep its test; un-hide the `[history-prefix]` cases (drop the `[.]` tag) so CTest runs them | D1, D5, D9 | not started |
| R8 Cache hygiene from M2 gaps: skill breakpoint placement, `prompt_cache_key` (D8), check `offered_tools` stability | D8 | not started |

## Phase 2: live confirmation (paid, needs D6)

One three-chat batch on Anthropic and one on OpenAI, before and after. Opus baseline exists in
`.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch/opus-batch/out-baseline/`. Measure cache reads vs cache
writes from the usage fields, plus answer quality via the eval harness. Add request-body logging
to the harness first (see M4) so the "after" run can be checked body by body, not only by tokens.

## Branches and worktrees

| Branch | Worktree | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | guard test commit; untracked `cache-rules.md` |
| `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | `.claude/worktrees/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | M3 fix commit |
| `claude/opus-cost-batch` | `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch` | uncommitted prototype + Anthropic harness switch; batch logs under `opus-batch/` |
| `claude/chat-history-cache` | `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache` | integration branch: guard test + M3 fix merged (`7c88fa2143`); phase 1 reverts land here |

## Side issue: 7 "MCP bridge" agent tests hang on HEAD

Found by M2 and M3 independently; unrelated to this work. The bridge's check that JusPrin is running never gets an answer from the in-process app server (`test_mcp_bridge.cpp:120`). The M3 session started a session of its own to look into it (`fix-mcp-bridge-tests-pro`, `local_45c7b710-9040-42f0-8e55-0b7952f1e540`); Kenneth did not ask for that one.

The MCP bridge hang is fixed on its own branch. The cause was a build setting: commit c177a160b3 left the bridge library compiled with a different Boost.Asio configuration than the rest of the test binary, so the bridge's connection waited on an event loop the test never ran. It's recorded in the plan doc; merging it is your call since you didn't ask for that work.

The history search for a chat-write latency measurement is still running. I'll report when it finishes.

# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (open)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | open |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes. Not neutral: the guard test shows that without the note, two consecutive assistant replies merge into one message on Anthropic | open |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | open |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | open |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Kenneth says it was decided against; no commit found yet, HEAD still accepts `set_chat_model` on the active chat | A thinking/effort change also restarts the cache on both providers (gap 6) | needs a pointer |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | open |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | open |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | open |
| D9 | Write cost of a larger chat record | Kenneth asked (2026-10-29) whether the latency / UI lock-up of writing large chat data to disk was ever measured. History search running; result goes here | gates D1 and R7 | searching |

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

| Task | Session | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Measure recorded requests | `cache-measure` | done | `chat-history-measurement.md`. No full live request bodies exist anywhere (the app has no request-body logging; the harness cut stored results at 4,000 chars). 26 scripted bodies in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` plus Opus usage lines were measured. See findings below. |
| M2 Byte-prefix invariant test + provider cache rules | `cache-invariant` | done | Commit `378b3037a0` on `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5`: two hidden Catch2 cases, tag `[history-prefix]`, both codecs, fail on HEAD (10/102 assertions), main case passes with the prototype, skills case fails where predicted (reminder at front, Responses drops the skill). `cache-rules.md` in that worktree root: cited rules, 9 gaps. Run: `agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`. |
| M3 Fix the Succeeded-to-Failed rewrite (handoff 4.9) | `tool-record-fix` | done, unmerged | Commit `cc5c12f9ff` on `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2`. Reproduced on HEAD. Fix: the save after a change is part of the outcome; the coordinator announces once, after the save; `fail()` throws `logic_error` on an announced record. 463 agent cases pass. 7 MCP bridge cases hang on HEAD too (pre-existing, not touched). |
| M4 Record an OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini) three-chat baseline before any revert | — | not started, needs D6 | Also needs request-body logging in the harness (M1: none exists); add it first so M4 and phase 2 produce bodies, not just usage lines. |

### M1 findings that change the plan

- **Never fired:** the 64 KiB trim. **Probably once:** the 16 KiB cut (bunny `object_analyze`, est. 17–19 KB, inference). Both are deletable without losing anything measured.
- **What actually changes at a turn start** (all inference on the split, no bodies): workspace blocks on each live result (1.0–1.7 KB each, ~60% of in-turn result bytes) and on the person's message; fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB); the plate picture (~1,050 Anthropic tokens); thinking; the reminder flip; the note.
- **Cost of retelling:** turn-start rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run, 3% with the prototype.
- **Two new leak candidates (not in the handoff):**
  - Skill text sits after the moving cache breakpoint, so it is billed uncached and written one request late (2,537 tokens per file-load turn, 441 per setup turn). Fix is a breakpoint placement, independent of the reverts.
  - `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` adds `object_import` only when the request has an importable attachment. On Anthropic tools come first, so a change there voids the whole cache. Not measured; needs a check.
- **Tokens per byte:** 2.7–3.4 bytes/token on this content, not 4; byte estimates understate tokens by 15–35%.

## Phase 1: reverts, one at a time, least behavioural change first

Each step: `[history-prefix]` guard + agent suite; steps that change what the model reads also run
the prompt eval harness on recorded cases. One session at a time on the Agent sources.

| Step | Depends on | Status |
|---|---|---|
| R0 Merge M3 (`cc5c12f9ff`) and the guard test (`378b3037a0`) onto a common branch | Kenneth's review | done 2026-10-29: `claude/chat-history-cache` at `7c88fa2143`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache`. Not merged to `jusprin-newui`, not pushed. |
| R1 Stop the file-load reminder flipping | D4 | not started |
| R2 Keep fired skills in the record on both providers; stop dropping them from the next OpenAI request | guard | not started |
| R3 Remove the 64 KiB rolling trim and the 16 KiB result cut; put the real limit in their place | D3 | not started |
| R4 Keep earlier messages' workspace blocks in the record | guard | not started |
| R5 Keep pictures in the record (blob references; ~1,050 Anthropic tokens each) | guard | not started |
| R6 Notes | D2 | not started |
| R7 Store each turn as sent, thinking included; delete the prototype's carry mechanism, keep its test; un-hide the `[history-prefix]` cases (drop the `[.]` tag) so CTest runs them | D1, D5, D9 | not started |
| R8 Cache hygiene from M2 gaps: skill breakpoint placement, `prompt_cache_key` (D8), check `offered_tools` stability | D8 | not started |

## Phase 2: live confirmation (paid, needs D6)

One three-chat batch on Anthropic and one on OpenAI, before and after. Opus baseline exists in
`.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch/opus-batch/out-baseline/`. Measure cache reads vs cache
writes from the usage fields, plus answer quality via the eval harness. Add request-body logging
to the harness first (see M4) so the "after" run can be checked body by body, not only by tokens.

|---|---|---|
| `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | guard test commit; untracked `cache-rules.md` |
| `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | `.claude/worktrees/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | M3 fix commit |
| `claude/opus-cost-batch` | `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch` | uncommitted prototype + Anthropic harness switch; batch logs under `opus-batch/` |
| `claude/chat-history-cache` | `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache` | integration branch: guard test + M3 fix merged (`7c88fa2143`); phase 1 reverts land here |

# Chat history cache: plan and progress

Working doc, 2026-10-29. Keep it untracked: never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.
Companion to `chat-history-cache-handoff.md` (the archaeology of every decision) and
`chat-history-measurement.md` (M1's numbers).

## Goal

The in-app Agent should resend earlier turns to the model exactly as it sent them, so the
provider's prompt cache covers the whole conversation, not just the system prompt and tools.
Both Anthropic and OpenAI stay supported. Every past optimization that makes the history change
is either reverted (when the revert simplifies the code and removes a cache-miss scenario) or
kept only after a measurement shows it does something.

## Decisions Kenneth owns (open)

| # | Decision | Proposal | What M1/M2 add | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | What the chat record holds | The exact request content as sent, per chat, thinking included (a chat is bound to one provider) | Thinking is part of the 3,500–9,000 tokens dropped at every turn start; Anthropic rejects edited history once thinking is carried (400 errors, accounts after 2026-08-31) | open |
| D2 | App notes in the project chat | Append where they happened, or never send them | A note is ~30 bytes. Not neutral: the guard test shows that without the note, two consecutive assistant replies merge into one message on Anthropic | open |
| D3 | Behaviour at the real context limit | Visible compaction that knowingly starts a new cache, or a refusal with a message. No rolling trim | The 64 KiB trim never fired in any recorded request (max replayed history ~27 KB); R3 is a plain deletion plus whatever D3 picks | open |
| D4 | File-load "data, not instructions" reminder | Delete it; the standing prompt has said the same since 86f8395071; keep the injection eval case | 215 bytes at the very front; flips on every chat; the guard test fails at messages[0] because of it | open |
| D5 | Mid-chat model switching | Kenneth says it was decided against; no commit found yet, HEAD still accepts `set_chat_model` on the active chat | A thinking/effort change also restarts the cache on both providers (gap 6) | needs a pointer |
| D6 | Spend approval for phase 2 live batches | ~$1.20 per Opus run, far less per OpenAI run; two runs each (before/after) | | open |
| D7 | Anthropic cache TTL: 5 min (1.25x write) or 1 hour (2x write) | Measurement question: the vase chat's 6-minute pause rewrote everything (13–21% of all cache writes in that run) | new from M2 gap 5 | open |
| D8 | `prompt_cache_key` per chat on OpenAI | Add it (project + chat id); without it all JusPrin users hash to the same machines and overflow above ~15 req/min | new from M2 gap 4; cheap, no behaviour change | open |
| D9 | Write cost of a larger chat record | Never measured. Searched git (`--all`), 148 memory notes, 1,055 Claude transcripts, 637 Codex sessions: every timing found is for mesh/3MF saves (autosave spike `279a14a75d`; Phase 4 benchmark at `67c190a40c`: whole 3MF save with embedded `state.json` ~180 ms for 220 KB, chat part not isolated; export-cost subagent 2026-09-10). The current design (`076ed1d4c3`, `autosave-version-history.md`) replaces the chat document atomically 1.5 s after the last change or within 15 s during a stream, and "Agent and project boundaries wait for the write"; no timing behind it. Proposal: M5, a timed test of `ProjectPersistence::commit()` on the main thread with documents of 1, 10 and 50 MB, before D1 is decided | gates D1 and R7 | open: needs M5 |

## Phase 0: ground truth (done)

| Task | Session | Status | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 Measure recorded requests | `cache-measure` | done | `chat-history-measurement.md`. No full live request bodies exist anywhere (the app has no request-body logging; the harness cut stored results at 4,000 chars). 26 scripted bodies in `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` plus Opus usage lines were measured. See findings below. |
| M2 Byte-prefix invariant test + provider cache rules | `cache-invariant` | done | Commit `378b3037a0` on `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5`: two hidden Catch2 cases, tag `[history-prefix]`, both codecs, fail on HEAD (10/102 assertions), main case passes with the prototype, skills case fails where predicted (reminder at front, Responses drops the skill). `cache-rules.md` in that worktree root: cited rules, 9 gaps. Run: `agent_bridge_tests "[history-prefix]"`. |
| M3 Fix the Succeeded-to-Failed rewrite (handoff 4.9) | `tool-record-fix` | done, unmerged | Commit `cc5c12f9ff` on `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2`. Reproduced on HEAD. Fix: the save after a change is part of the outcome; the coordinator announces once, after the save; `fail()` throws `logic_error` on an announced record. 463 agent cases pass. 7 MCP bridge cases hang on HEAD too (pre-existing, not touched). |
| M4 Record an OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini) three-chat baseline before any revert | — | not started, needs D6 | Also needs request-body logging in the harness (M1: none exists); add it first so M4 and phase 2 produce bodies, not just usage lines. |

### M1 findings that change the plan

- **Never fired:** the 64 KiB trim. **Probably once:** the 16 KiB cut (bunny `object_analyze`, est. 17–19 KB, inference). Both are deletable without losing anything measured.
- **What actually changes at a turn start** (all inference on the split, no bodies): workspace blocks on each live result (1.0–1.7 KB each, ~60% of in-turn result bytes) and on the person's message; fired skill text (1.3–8.5 KB); the plate picture (~1,050 Anthropic tokens); thinking; the reminder flip; the note.
- **Cost of retelling:** turn-start rewrites were 24% of all cache-write tokens in the baseline run, 3% with the prototype.
- **Two new leak candidates (not in the handoff):**
  - Skill text sits after the moving cache breakpoint, so it is billed uncached and written one request late (2,537 tokens per file-load turn, 441 per setup turn). Fix is a breakpoint placement, independent of the reverts.
  - `offered_tools` in `ProviderAgent.cpp` adds `object_import` only when the request has an importable attachment. On Anthropic tools come first, so a change there voids the whole cache. Not measured; needs a check.
- **Tokens per byte:** 2.7–3.4 bytes/token on this content, not 4; byte estimates understate tokens by 15–35%.

## Phase 1: reverts, one at a time, least behavioural change first

Each step: `[history-prefix]` guard + agent suite; steps that change what the model reads also run
the prompt eval harness on recorded cases. One session at a time on the Agent sources.

| Step | Depends on | Status |
|---|---|---|
| R0 Merge M3 (`cc5c12f9ff`) and the guard test (`378b3037a0`) onto a common branch | Kenneth's review | done 2026-10-29: `claude/chat-history-cache` at `7c88fa2143`, worktree `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache`. Not merged to `jusprin-newui`, not pushed. |
| R1 Stop the file-load reminder flipping | D4 | not started |
| R2 Keep fired skills in the record on both providers; stop dropping them from the next OpenAI request | guard | not started |
| R3 Remove the 64 KiB rolling trim and the 16 KiB result cut; put the real limit in their place | D3 | not started |
| R4 Keep earlier messages' workspace blocks in the record | guard | not started |
| R5 Keep pictures in the record (blob references; ~1,050 Anthropic tokens each) | guard | not started |
| R6 Notes | D2 | not started |
| R7 Store each turn as sent, thinking included; delete the prototype's carry mechanism, keep its test; un-hide the `[history-prefix]` cases (drop the `[.]` tag) so CTest runs them | D1, D5, D9 | not started |
| R8 Cache hygiene from M2 gaps: skill breakpoint placement, `prompt_cache_key` (D8), check `offered_tools` stability | D8 | not started |

## Phase 2: live confirmation (paid, needs D6)

One three-chat batch on Anthropic and one on OpenAI, before and after. Opus baseline exists in
`.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch/opus-batch/out-baseline/`. Measure cache reads vs cache
writes from the usage fields, plus answer quality via the eval harness. Add request-body logging
to the harness first (see M4) so the "after" run can be checked body by body, not only by tokens.

## Branches and worktrees

| Branch | Worktree | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `claude/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | `.claude/worktrees/cache-invariant-test-51dab5` | guard test commit; untracked `cache-rules.md` |
| `claude/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | `.claude/worktrees/tool-record-terminal-0b61d2` | M3 fix commit |
| `claude/opus-cost-batch` | `.claude/worktrees/opus-cost-batch` | uncommitted prototype + Anthropic harness switch; batch logs under `opus-batch/` |
| `claude/chat-history-cache` | `.claude/worktrees/chat-history-cache` | integration branch: guard test + M3 fix merged (`7c88fa2143`); phase 1 reverts land here |

## Side issue: 7 "MCP bridge" agent tests hang on HEAD

Found by M2 and M3 independently; unrelated to this work. The bridge's check that JusPrin is running never gets an answer from the in-process app server (`test_mcp_bridge.cpp:120`). The M3 session started a session of its own to look into it (`fix-mcp-bridge-tests-pro`, `local_45c7b710-9040-42f0-8e55-0b7952f1e540`); Kenneth did not ask for that one. Outcome: fixed in `8f18a22dc8` on `claude/dreamy-ramanujan-fcaede` (5-line change to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/Bridge/CMakeLists.txt`): `c177a160b3` left the bridge library compiled with a different Boost.Asio setting than the rest of the test binary. Not merged, not pushed; Kenneth decides.

The answer is no. Nobody has ever measured what writing the chat record to disk costs the UI.

**What was searched.** Git history across all branches, the 148 memory notes, 1,055 Claude Code transcripts and 637 Codex sessions, scanned for persistence and chat-document terms near timing words. The scans were keyword-gated, so a measurement phrased differently could have been missed, but nothing surfaced.

**What exists instead.** Every timing found is for mesh or 3MF work:

- The autosave spike of 2026-09-29 timed Orca's 3MF saves blocking the main thread. No chat data was involved.
- The Phase 4 benchmark of 2026-08-30 timed a whole project save at about 180 ms for 220 KB. That archive embedded the chat state, but the chat part was never isolated, and that design was replaced by the managed folder a month later.
- An export-cost measurement of 2026-09-10 timed 3MF exports against triangle count, with no chat content.

**What the current design assumes without a number.** The chat document is replaced atomically 1.5 seconds after the last change, or within 15 seconds during a stream, and the design doc says Agent and project boundaries wait for that write. The handoff's own words on the plate picture were that its size "was never measured". So if D1 makes the record hold every request as sent, the write grows by the pictures and tool results, and nothing tells us whether the boundary wait becomes visible.

**Proposal, recorded as M5.** A timed test of the persistence commit on the main thread with chat documents of 1, 10 and 50 MB, run before D1 is decided. It needs no model call and builds in minutes.

<cross-session-message from="local_97f342dd-4367-4bc5-830d-1c6d6d91db47" from-name="Chat history cache handoff">
Kenneth approved a design for roles and lifetimes in the Agent chat request (decided in a forked side session, 2026-10-29); please update chat-history-cache-plan.md and the tracker accordingly.

Kenneth's words: "ok. go with your proposal. tell the main session to update the plan and tracker accordingly."

What was decided (fills D1, D2, D4, and adds a frame for R2/R6/R7):

1. Append-only record, separate from visibility. Each chat keeps an append-only record of every item ever sent to the model. A request renders that record plus the new items. No item is rewritten, dropped or re-derived. What the model should still see is a lifetime flag per item, never an edit of the record. Source: Anthropic's mid-conversation system messages doc (platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages): a cleared message "stays in the array but renders nothing", must be "re-sent verbatim", and rebuilding or dropping it "is an edit to an earlier message" that fails the thinking check and breaks the cache.

2. Three roles, assigned by who speaks, never by lifetime:
   - Operator, standing: top-level `system` field / Responses `instructions`. Standing prompt and tools, written once per chat, never changed.
   - Operator, in conversation: Anthropic in-array `role:"system"` message (Opus 5.5 and 5.x, not Sonnet 5); OpenAI `developer` item. Carries BOTH situational instructions (skills, the file-load reminder if it survives) AND app observations (notes: slice finished, hand setup change, calibration handover). Justification from the doc: a user message "is treated as coming from the end user, whereas a system message is treated as coming from you, the application operator"; "state changes your application observes" is a named use case. This replaces today's "JusPrin app note, not the person's words" user-text prefix.
   - End user: `user` role carries the person's words plus what travels with them (workspace block, plate picture, file report). Kept in the record as sent (closes R4).
   - Tool results stay in their own channel (tool_result / function_call_output), never promoted; the doc forbids relaying third-party content through system messages.

3. Lifetimes: skills and the reminder clear at the next user message on Anthropic (`clear_at: "next_user_message"`, beta header `mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21`); on OpenAI there is no clear, so they stay visible and should be kept short. Notes the model replied to stay visible on both. Thinking/reasoning is stored per chat and replayed (D1: record holds exact content as sent; pictures as blob references, never inline base64).

4. Consequences for the tracker:
   - D1 decided: exact request content as sent, thinking included, pictures as blob refs.
   - D2 decided: notes become operator-role in-conversation messages, kept in the record, never cleared; one treatment for project and printer chat.
   - D4: reminder is either deleted (standing prompt already says it) or becomes a turn-scoped system message like a skill; Kenneth has not picked between the two.

# Global Claude Code Rules

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.
